summary: Checkpoint: a finite weighted prime-truncation API and explicit first/second arithmetic-moment comparisons. nodes.title: Finite weighted prime truncation
nodes.statement: Construct S(P,a) : ArithmeticFunction real for a finite set P of natural indices and real weights a. Set S(P,a)(0)=0 and, for n>0, S(P,a)(n)=sum_{p in P} (if p divides n then a(p) else 0). Only the arithmetic interpretation and the prime-power/coprime laws require every member of P to be prime.
hypotheses: P is a finite set; a is real-valued.
proofSteps: Use the existing ArithmeticFunction=ZeroHom carrier. Define the function by the displayed zero guard and finite sum; check its zero field by evaluation.
Export positive evaluation before using the construction in averages. Prove the seven separate API nodes below; do not add an independent arithmetic-function or probability carrier.
acceptance: Zero, positive and empty evaluations agree with the stated convention.
Implement the five tests listed on this node; multiplication in ArithmeticFunction is not used for pointwise products.

api.name: primeDivisibilitySum_apply
api.statement: For n>0, S(P,a)(n)=sum over p in P of a(p) times the indicator of p dividing n.

api.name: primeDivisibilitySum_empty
api.statement: S(empty,a)=0 as an ArithmeticFunction, including at n=0.

api.name: primeDivisibilitySum_congr
api.statement: If a(p)=b(p) for p in P then S(P,a)=S(P,b).

api.name: primeDivisibilitySum_add
api.statement: S(P,a+b)=S(P,a)+S(P,b), where the additions are pointwise.

api.name: primeDivisibilitySum_mul_of_coprime
api.statement: For prime P and coprime positive m,n, S(P,a)(mn)=S(P,a)(m)+S(P,a)(n).

api.name: primeDivisibilitySum_prime_pow
api.statement: For prime P, prime q and k>=1, S(P,a)(q^k)=a(q) if q is in P, and 0 otherwise.

api.name: primeDivisibilitySum_primeFactors
api.statement: S(n.primeFactors,constant 1)(n) equals the real cast of the existing cardDistinctFactors n, for every natural n.

nodes.title: Coprime product law
nodes.statement: For prime P and coprime positive m,n, S(P,a)(mn)=S(P,a)(m)+S(P,a)(n).
hypotheses: Every p in P is prime; m,n>0; gcd(m,n)=1.
proofSteps: For p in P, primality gives p divides mn iff p divides m or p divides n.
The two events cannot both hold: a common prime divisor would divide gcd(m,n)=1. Thus their 0/1 indicators add without a double contribution.
Multiply by a(p), sum, and apply positive evaluation at m,n,mn.
acceptance: For P={2}, a(2)=2, m=n=2, the identity fails: the coprimality hypothesis cannot be removed.

nodes.title: Prime-power law
nodes.statement: For prime P, prime q and k>=1, S(P,a)(q^k)=a(q) if q is in P, and 0 otherwise.
hypotheses: All p in P are prime; q prime; k>=1.
proofSteps: For p in P, p divides q^k iff p divides q, using the prime divisor-of-power theorem and its elementary converse.
Since p and q are prime this holds iff p=q. The finite sum has at most the q summand.
acceptance: At P={2,3}, weights a(p)=p, evaluate q=2,k=3 to 2 and q=5,k=1 to 0.

nodes.title: Compatibility with the existing omega
nodes.statement: S(n.primeFactors,constant 1)(n) equals the real cast of the existing cardDistinctFactors n, for every natural n.
hypotheses: n is any natural number, including 0 and 1.
proofSteps: At n=0 the existing arithmetic-function zero laws give both sides zero.
At positive n each member of n.primeFactors divides n, so the sum is the cardinal of n.primeFactors.
Identify that finite set with the deduplicated prime-factor list and use the existing cardDistinctFactors_apply theorem.
acceptance: At 12 the value is 2; at 0 and 1 it is 0. Never substitute the multiplicity-counting Omega.

nodes.title: Exact divisibility probability
nodes.statement: For every positive d, the real probability mu_N({n : d divides n}) equals (Nat.div N d)/N. This is a probability specialization of existing counting, not a new multiples-counting theorem.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
proofSteps: Apply empiricalMeasure_apply_toReal to the measurable divisibility set on discrete naturals.
Its indicator sum is the real cast of the number of k<N with d dividing k+1. Substitute the already proved Nat.card_multiples and move the finite natural cast through the sum.
acceptance: N=5,d=2 gives 2/5; d>N gives 0; d=1 gives 1.

nodes.title: Signed finite counting error
nodes.statement: Let e_N(d)=mu_N(d divides n)-1/d, in the reals. For d>0, e_N(d)=-(N mod d)/(N*d), so -1/N<e_N(d)<=0; in particular |e_N(d)|<=1/N. This notation is a local expression, not another probability definition.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
proofSteps: Write N=d*(Nat.div N d)+(N mod d) with 0<=N mod d<d.
Substitute the exact probability, cast the quotient-remainder equality to the reals, and divide by positive N*d.
The sign and strict lower bound follow from the remainder bounds. Retain the sign for exact-period specialization.
acceptance: N=5,d=2 gives -1/10. If d divides N the error is exactly zero.

nodes.title: Joint divisibility and the lcm
nodes.statement: For positive d,e, mu_N({n : d divides n and e divides n})=(Nat.div N (Nat.lcm d e))/N. For distinct primes p,q, the denominator inside Nat.div becomes p*q; for equal primes it is p, not p^2.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
proofSteps: The joint event is exactly the event that lcm(d,e) divides n, by the defining universal property of lcm. This lcm is positive.
Apply divisibility-probability. Use Coprime.lcm_eq_mul only when coprimality has been proved; distinct primes are coprime since a common divisor is 1 or each of them.
acceptance: N=12,d=4,e=6 gives 1/12 rather than floor(12/24)/12=0.
N=5,p=2,q=3 gives 0 while the product of marginal probabilities is 2/25.

nodes.title: Exact mean of a finite truncation
nodes.statement: For prime P and real a, integral S(P,a) dmu_N = sum_{p in P} a(p)*(Nat.div N p)/N. All the quantities are real.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
P finite, all its members prime; a real-valued.
proofSteps: Apply integral_empiricalMeasure to S(P,a); on the discrete natural carrier it is strongly measurable.
For k<N, k+1>0, so use positive-evaluation. Interchange the two finite sums.
For each p, the sum of divisibility indicators is Nat.card_multiples N p. Pull out the constant real weight. No independence enters the proof.

nodes.statement: Write A=sum_{p in P} a(p)/p and L=sum_{p in P}|a(p)|. Then |integral S(P,a) dmu_N-A|<=L/N.

nodes.title: Exact centered pair average
nodes.statement: For positive p,q, let I_d(n) be the real 0/1 indicator of d dividing n. Then integral (I_p-1/p)*(I_q-1/q) dmu_N equals (Nat.div N (Nat.lcm p q))/N -(Nat.div N p)/(N*q) -(Nat.div N q)/(N*p)+1/(p*q).
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
p,q>0; primality is not needed for this identity.
proofSteps: Convert the integral to its finite average and expand the product into four terms.
The product I_p*I_q is the indicator of the joint divisibility event; the constant term averages to itself because there are exactly N terms.
Use divisibility-probability and joint-divisibility for the three nonconstant terms.
acceptance: When p=q use I_p^2=I_p. When N=5,p=2,q=3 the centered average is -1/15.

nodes.title: Uniform prime-pair error
nodes.statement: For primes p,q, put D(p,q)=1/p-1/p^2 when p=q, and 0 otherwise. Then |integral (I_p-1/p)*(I_q-1/q) dmu_N-D(p,q)|<=2/N. Repeated primes are included.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
p,q prime.
proofSteps: Replace each floor probability in centered-pair-identity by 1/d+e_N(d).
If p=q then lcm(p,p)=p, and the nonerror part is 1/p-1/p^2. If p!=q, coprimality gives lcm(p,q)=p*q and the nonerror part is zero.
The remaining expression is e_N(lcm(p,q))-e_N(p)/q-e_N(q)/p. Each error has magnitude at most 1/N.
Since p,q>=2, 1+1/p+1/q<=2. The triangle inequality proves the bound, including the diagonal.
acceptance: At p=q=2, the centered square equals 1/4 pointwise and the error is actually zero.
Distinct-prime indicators under mu_N need not be independent.

nodes.title: Finite-head second-moment comparison
nodes.statement: For prime P and real a, write A=sum a(p)/p, L=sum |a(p)|, V=sum a(p)^2*(1/p-1/p^2). Then |integral (S(P,a)-A)^2 dmu_N - V| <= 2*L^2/N. This is a centered second moment about A, not a formula for variance about the empirical mean.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
P finite and prime; a real-valued, with no sign or boundedness hypothesis beyond finiteness of P.
proofSteps: For n in the positive sample, S(P,a)(n)-A=sum a(p)*(I_p(n)-1/p).
Square and distribute as a double sum over all ordered pairs (p,q), including the diagonal. Convert the integral to a finite average and interchange these finite sums.
Subtract the sum of a(p)*a(q)*D(p,q). Its off-diagonal terms vanish and its diagonal is exactly V.
Apply centered-pair-error and the triangle inequality, obtaining (2/N)*sum_{p,q}|a(p)|*|a(q)|=(2/N)*L^2. No probabilistic independence or central limit theorem is used.
acceptance: P empty gives 0=0. Signed weights and repeated pair indices must survive expansion.
The bound is useful only when L^2/N is controlled; it is not the Turan-Kubilius inequality and does not discharge the large-prime tail of Erdos-Kac.

nodes.title: Exact moments on complete prime periods
nodes.statement: Under the second-moment-comparison hypotheses, assume Q=product_{p in P}p divides N. Then integral (S(P,a)-A)^2 dmu_N=V. Also the already stated weighted-mean formula gives integral S(P,a) dmu_N=A, so this centered moment is the actual variance in this case.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
P finite and prime; a real-valued; product_{p in P}p divides N.
proofSteps: Each p in P divides Q and thus N. For p,q in P their lcm divides Q, whether p=q or not.
All three remainder terms in the centered-pair-identity are zero. The exact pair average is D(p,q).
Repeat the explicit finite double-sum argument of second-moment-comparison with equality. The exact first moment follows by replacing each floor quotient by N/p in weighted-mean.
acceptance: For N=6,P={2,3},a(p)=p, A=2 and V=3. For N=5 the corresponding mean is 7/5 and centered second moment is 9/5, so completeness of the period cannot be silently removed.
For P empty, Q=1; every positive N satisfies the condition and both moments vanish.
